questions.stem: Explain how static typing can prevent errors in a program compared to dynamic typing.
markingGuide: Static typing checks types at compile time.
Errors are caught before the program runs.
Prevents type mismatch errors that could occur at runtime.
Dynamic typing checks types at runtime, potentially leading to runtime errors.
questions.explanation: Static typing enforces type checks at compile time, ensuring that type-related errors are caught early. This prevents type mismatch errors that could cause runtime failures in dynamically typed languages, which only check types during execution.
